reason: The regular people of Shechem and surrounding areas are consistently portrayed negatively throughout this passage from Judges 9. They are depicted as morally compromised (funding the murder of 70 brothers), easily manipulated by rhetoric (first trusting Abimelech, then Gaal), disloyal (betraying their leaders), foolish in governance (making poor choices about kingship), and ultimately deserving of divine punishment (1000 die in the tower; God returns their own evil upon their heads). The text emphasizes their weakness of character, susceptibility to base desires (festivals, eating, drinking, cursing), and complicity in violence. The conclusion explicitly states that God brought the evil of the men of Shechem back upon their own heads as a judgment. This is a decidedly unfavorable portrayal.
